title: Human Vagus Nerve Collection and Histology Microscopy Protocol
author: Nicole A. Pelot
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bh4cj8sw
materials: We rinsed each sample with deionized water.
We rinsed the slides in distilled water.

steps.title: Collect Cervical Vagus Nerve Samples
steps.instruction: Collect 2 cm bilateral cervical vagus nerve samples at the midlevel of the thyroid cartilage (where a line from the rostral end of the sternum to the earlobe intersects the nerve).

substeps.instruction: Measure from the 'valley' of the common carotid bifurcation to the center of each sample.

steps.title: Collect Subdiaphragmatic Vagus Nerve Samples
steps.instruction: Collect samples of the anterior and posterior subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve trunks along the esophagus between the diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus and the gastroesophageal junction.

steps.title: Orient and Fix Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare samples for processing to maintain orientation and ensure fixation.

substeps.instruction: Dye the rostral end of each sample green.
Place each sample between two histology sponges in a mega-sized histology cassette.
Store cassettes in a tub with 4% paraformaldehyde in a 4 °C refrigerator.

steps.title: Process Tissue
steps.instruction: Process samples using the long cycle in a Leica ASP300S Tissue Processor for approximately 10 hours.

substeps.instruction: Clearite: 50 min, three times.
Paraffin wax: 50 min, three times.

steps.title: Embed and Section Tissue
steps.instruction: Embed and section the processed nerve samples.

substeps.instruction: Cut each sample in half transversely.
Embed halves together cut side down in paraffin to allow transverse sectioning from the center outward.
Collect 5 µm sections, placing two serial sections per microscope slide for fifteen slides.

steps.title: Dry and Bake Slides
steps.instruction: Prepare slides for staining through drying and heating.

substeps.instruction: Air dry slides overnight at room temperature.
Bake slides at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Slides for Masson's Trichrome
steps.instruction: Perform initial preparation on slides 2 and 14 of the 15-slide set.

substeps.instruction: Bake slides at 60 °C for 1.5 hours.
Cool slides overnight.
Deparaffinize and hydrate to distilled water: xylene (2x 6 min), 100% ethanol (5 min), 95% ethanol (4 min), 70% ethanol (3 min), dH2O (2x 1 min).

steps.title: Perform Masson's Trichrome Staining
steps.instruction: Execute the staining sequence for the selected slides.

substeps.instruction: Place slides in Bouin's fixative (mordant) at room temperature overnight.
Wash in running tap water until yellow color disappears (~10 minutes).
Place in Weigert's Iron Hematoxylin solution for 10 min.
Wash in running tap water for 10 min.
Place in Biebrich Scarlet-Acid Fuchsin solution for 5 min.
Wash in running tap water for 2 min.
Place in Phosphomolybdic-Phosphotungstic Acid solution for 10 min.
Transfer directly to Aniline Blue solution for 3 min.
Differentiate counterstain (A. blue) in 1% Acetic Acid solution for 1 min.
Dehydrate and clear: 95% ethanol (1 min), 100% ethanol (4 min), xylene (5 min).
Coverslip the slides.

steps.title: Image Samples
steps.instruction: Capture images of the processed samples using a Nikon Ti2 microscope with a Photometrics Prime 95B-25MM camera.

substeps.instruction: Image each sample at 10x.
Select the best of four slices per sample based on quality (absence of tearing or fraying).
